title: Refinance
intro: Should you refinance a loan? How much the property supports, the rate, the lender’s limits, a new loan or an extension with today’s lender — and several properties under one new loan.

topics.title: Open a refinance
topics.intro: A refinance starts from a loan’s page: pick the property, then “Refi Calculator”.

steps.title: Refi Calculator on the loan’s page
steps.text: Open a loan (click its property on the Portfolio tab, or pick it under Specific Property). Its page has a row of buttons at the top; “Refi Calculator” opens the refinance analysis for that loan.

marks.label: Refi Calculator
marks.text: Opens the refinance analysis for the loan on this page. Nothing changes until you save something there.

steps.title: The refinance screen
steps.text: The refinance opens in place of the loan’s page. Everything on it is worked out live: change any box and the answers update at once. Your choices for this refinance (the lender’s limits, an appraisal, the kind of deal) are kept with the property for the whole team.

marks.label: Refinance Analysis
marks.text: The loan being looked at, and the question: should you refinance?

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Back to the loan’s page. Nothing is saved by closing (your limits and appraisal stay).

marks.label: Save as a loan
marks.text: Shown when there is a loan to propose. Saves the proposed loan as a new loan and marks today’s loan paid off (refinanced) — it asks first. Here it also says the cash you would pay in.

marks.label: Refi Calculator (greyed)
marks.text: Greyed while the refinance is open. Close takes you back to the loan’s page.

marks.label: What kind of deal?
marks.text: A new loan, or an extension with today’s lender — see the next topics.

topics.title: Today’s loan and the kind of deal
topics.intro: What you owe today, and whether you are looking at a new loan or an extension with today’s lender.

steps.title: Current Loan
steps.text: The facts of today’s loan, from its record.

marks.label: Payoff balance
marks.text: What you owe today — the amount a new loan has to pay off.

marks.label: Current rate
marks.text: Today’s interest rate on the loan.

marks.label: Monthly P&I
marks.text: Today’s monthly principal and interest payment.

marks.label: Remaining
marks.text: Months until today’s loan ends.

marks.label: Matures
marks.text: The date today’s loan is due.

marks.label: Rate reset
marks.text: For a hybrid loan: when the fixed rate ends, what it resets to and the new payment.

steps.title: What kind of deal?
steps.text: Pick this first — everything below it follows your choice. A new loan pays off today’s loan with a new one; an extension keeps today’s lender on new terms. Each keeps its own limits, so switching back and forth loses nothing.

marks.label: New loan
marks.text: The verdict, the lender’s limits and the payment schedule below are a new loan’s — it replaces today’s loan(s).

marks.label: Extend with today’s lender
marks.text: Judge an extension instead: today’s lender keeps the loan on new terms, perhaps after a pay-down (the topic “Extend with today’s lender”).

topics.title: Coverage & value today
topics.intro: How today’s loan stands: the NOI it is measured on, coverage, value, the credit tier, the cost to pay it off early, and the capital stack.

steps.title: Coverage & value — today’s loan
steps.text: Today’s loan measured on the property’s NOI. These are the figures a lender looks at first.

marks.label: Annual NOI
marks.text: The property’s yearly net operating income this analysis uses (here typed on the loan).

marks.label: Cap rate
marks.text: Used to estimate the value: value = NOI ÷ cap rate.

marks.label: Est. value
marks.text: The estimated value of the property (an appraisal you type replaces it — see “How much the property supports”).

marks.label: LTV today
marks.text: Loan-to-value: what you owe ÷ the value.

marks.label: Debt service today
marks.text: A year of today’s payments.

marks.label: DSCR today
marks.text: Debt coverage: NOI ÷ a year of payments. Lenders usually want 1.25× or more.

marks.label: Interest-only DSCR
marks.text: Coverage on an interest-only payment — what some lenders size on.

marks.label: Debt yield today
marks.text: NOI ÷ what you owe — what insurance companies and CMBS lenders look at.

marks.label: Coverage today
marks.text: Whether today’s coverage clears your DSCR floor.

marks.label: Edit inputs
marks.text: Opens a small window to keep or change the NOI and the cap rate (next step).

marks.label: Credit tier
marks.text: How a lender would grade today’s numbers. Below the floor, the line under it says which test fails; a strong tier takes basis points off the proposed spread.

marks.label: Why it is below the floor
marks.text: Each test that fails, against your floor or ceiling: DSCR, LTV, debt yield. Shown only when a test fails.

marks.label: Exit cost — penalty type
marks.text: How the early-payoff penalty is worked out — explained in the next steps.

marks.label: Exit cost
marks.text: The early-payoff penalty in dollars today (and as a % of the balance).

marks.label: Capital stack
marks.text: Link a mezz or senior loan on the same property — explained below.

marks.label: How these are worked out
marks.text: The formulas behind the figures above. They are screening estimates — confirm with the loan documents and a rate sheet.

steps.title: Edit inputs — the NOI and the cap rate
steps.text: “Edit inputs” shows the NOI saved for the property and its cap rate. Keep them, or change them.

marks.label: Saved annual NOI
marks.text: The NOI this property already has.

marks.label: Cap rate
marks.text: The cap rate used for the value.

marks.label: Change it
marks.text: Shows boxes to type a new NOI and cap rate (next step).

marks.label: Keep & continue
marks.text: Closes the window and keeps both as they are.

steps.title: Typing a new NOI
steps.text: Type the yearly NOI in dollars and, if you have a better figure, the cap rate. The new NOI becomes the property’s from now on.

marks.label: Property annual NOI
marks.text: The yearly net operating income, from the operating statement or rent roll.

marks.label: Cap rate (%)
marks.text: Value = NOI ÷ cap rate; it sets the loan-to-value.

marks.label: Continue
marks.text: Saves both and updates the whole analysis.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Closes without changing anything.

steps.title: Exit cost — the early-payoff penalty
steps.text: Paying today’s loan off early usually costs a penalty. The app estimates it from the type of penalty in the loan; “assumed” means nobody has confirmed the type yet.

marks.label: Penalty type
marks.text: Yield Maintenance (the default), Step-down (a % of the balance that falls each year), Defeasance (a quoted figure), or Open / at par (no penalty). Picking one confirms it and saves it on the loan.

marks.label: Assumed
marks.text: Shown until you pick the type: the estimate uses yield maintenance.

marks.label: Prepay basis
marks.text: How the estimate was worked out (for yield maintenance: today’s Treasury, the months left, the 1% floor).

marks.label: Exit cost
marks.text: The estimated penalty in dollars — confirm the real figure from the loan documents.

marks.label: As % of balance
marks.text: The same penalty as a share of what you owe.

steps.title: Step-down and defeasance
steps.text: A step-down penalty asks for this year’s % of the balance; a defeasance takes the figure you were quoted (until you type one, a yield-maintenance estimate stands in).

marks.label: Step-down
marks.text: Picked here.

marks.label: This year’s step-down
marks.text: Type this year’s % (for example 3 in year 1 of a 3-2-1 schedule). The exit cost follows.

steps.title: Defeasance — the quoted figure
steps.text: Type the defeasance figure from the lender or the consultant; the box shows the yield-maintenance estimate until you do.

marks.label: Defeasance
marks.text: Picked here.

marks.label: Quoted figure
marks.text: The defeasance cost you were quoted, in dollars.

steps.title: Capital stack
steps.text: When the property also has a mezzanine (or senior) loan, link it here: leverage and coverage are then read on the combined debt.

marks.label: Link a loan
marks.text: Pick the other loan on the same property (None = this loan alone). Agency senior loans don’t allow subordinate debt.

steps.title: The NOI basis — which NOI the refinance uses
steps.text: Once a property has a T12, the refinance can be measured on different NOIs. Here Villages of Whitewater has a made-up T12 and a pro forma: pick the NOI you want the loan sized on — everything below follows.

marks.label: In-place T12
marks.text: The NOI as the property runs today, from its T12 (by the T12 rule).

marks.label: Underwritten
marks.text: The NOI the Underwriting tab works out with your assumptions — the figure a lender underwrites to.

marks.label: Pro forma · Safe
marks.text: The pro forma NOI (Underwriting → Pro forma): the T12 with your changes, each with its story. Shown when the pro forma adds up.

marks.label: Pro forma · Aggressive
marks.text: The Aggressive version — shown when it has changes of its own.

marks.label: Which months
marks.text: The months of the T12 the NOI comes from.

marks.label: What it is sized on
marks.text: Says which NOI the whole analysis now uses — the verdict, the limits and the amount all follow your pick.

topics.title: What to push — test it against the refinance
topics.intro: Tick a move Claude suggested, or add your own, and see what it does to the refinance.

steps.title: Claude’s moves and your own levers
steps.text: Claude’s suggestions from “What to push” in Underwriting appear here as tick boxes, each with its yearly effect on the NOI. Ticking one adds it to the NOI this refinance uses — coverage, the credit tier and the verdict update at once. It is a what-if: nothing is saved.

marks.label: A move
marks.text: Tick to add its estimated yearly effect to the NOI used here; untick to take it out.

marks.label: Its yearly effect
marks.text: What the move adds to the in-place NOI and to the underwritten NOI. Ticking it adds the one that matches the NOI basis picked above (here underwritten).

marks.label: Your own lever — name
marks.text: A name for something you expect to add (for example paid parking).

marks.label: Your own lever — dollars a year
marks.text: The yearly amount it adds (a negative amount takes NOI away).

marks.label: Add
marks.text: Adds your lever to the list, ticked.

steps.title: Ticked — the NOI moves
steps.text: With a move ticked and a lever of your own added, the card says how much is added to the working NOI.

marks.label: Applied
marks.text: How much the ticked moves add to the NOI this refinance uses.

marks.label: Ticked move
marks.text: Counted now.

marks.label: Your lever
marks.text: Marked “yours”; tick or untick it like Claude’s.
Removes your lever.

topics.title: The verdict — can you, should you?
topics.intro: The coloured box answers two questions in order: can the property support a loan the size of what you owe, and is it worth doing.

steps.title: Act before … — pay down
steps.text: Queens Gate’s rate resets within 12 months and the property can’t support what you owe. The box says so first, with the date, and what it takes: the pay-down to refinance at these limits, or an extension with today’s lender.

marks.label: The answer
marks.text: Act before the reset — pay down $X. (Other answers: Refinance, Your decision, Don’t refinance.)

marks.label: You owe (payoff)
marks.text: What a new loan has to pay off.

marks.label: Property supports
marks.text: The biggest loan the property supports at the proposed rate and the lender’s limits.

marks.label: Today’s loan rate
marks.text: With the reset ahead (what it resets to, and when).

marks.label: Proposed loan rate
marks.text: The new loan’s rate, from the rate boxes below.

marks.label: When
marks.text: What is ending: the rate reset (with the new payment) or the maturity.

marks.label: To refinance
marks.text: The pay-down a new loan needs: what you owe less what the property supports.

marks.label: To extend
marks.text: The pay-down today’s lender would need — pick “Extend with today’s lender” to work it out.

marks.label: Proposed rate
marks.text: The new loan’s rate type, index and spread — see “The proposed rate and amount”.

marks.label: Proposed loan amount
marks.text: Starts at what the property supports; type a smaller amount to test it. The line under it shows that loan’s coverage, LTV and debt yield.

marks.label: Can you?
marks.text: Stage one: can the property support a loan the size of what you owe? Here no — and why.

marks.label: How “supports $X” is worked out
marks.text: The NOI, rate, payment and value behind the figure, and the lender’s four limits — see “How much the property supports”.

marks.label: Bottom line
marks.text: What to do, in one line.

steps.title: Refinance
steps.text: The Mews at Princeton, with the lender’s spread typed as 0 for the example: the property supports more than you owe, and the lower rate saves more interest than the early-payoff penalty — so: Refinance.

marks.label: Refinance
marks.text: Both answers are yes.

marks.label: You owe (payoff)
marks.text: What a new loan has to pay off.

marks.label: Property supports
marks.text: The biggest loan the property supports at the proposed rate and the lender’s limits.

marks.label: Today’s loan rate
marks.text: The rate today’s loan charges now.

marks.label: Proposed loan rate
marks.text: The new loan’s rate, from the rate boxes below.

marks.label: Proposed rate
marks.text: The new loan’s rate type, index and spread — see “The proposed rate and amount”.

marks.label: Proposed loan amount
marks.text: Type a smaller amount to test it. The line under it shows that loan’s coverage, LTV and debt yield.

marks.label: Can you? Yes
marks.text: The property supports at least what you owe.

marks.label: How “supports $X” is worked out
marks.text: The NOI, rate, payment and value behind the figure, and the lender’s four limits — see “How much the property supports”.

marks.label: Should you? Yes
marks.text: Your rule: the new rate saves more interest (until today’s loan ends) than the penalty — or today’s loan ends within 12 months anyway. When the saving doesn’t cover the penalty but the property can refinance, the box turns amber: “Your decision”.

marks.label: Refinance.
marks.text: The proposed loan appears below, with “Save as a loan” at the top.

steps.title: Your decision
steps.text: Still The Mews at Princeton, now with a 20 bps spread and a bigger loan of $135,000,000 (made-up figures). The lower rate no longer saves as much as the early-payoff penalty — but the new loan pays out more than 20% of what you owe in cash, even after the penalty. So the app doesn’t decide for you: it shows both choices. (With the same rate and a loan only the size of what you owe, the answer is Don’t refinance.)

marks.label: Your decision
marks.text: The property can refinance, and it is worth it only for the cash.

marks.label: You owe (payoff)
marks.text: What a new loan has to pay off.

marks.label: Property supports
marks.text: The biggest loan the property supports at the proposed rate and the lender’s limits.

marks.label: Today’s loan rate
marks.text: The rate today’s loan charges now.

marks.label: Proposed loan rate
marks.text: The new loan’s rate, from the rate boxes below.

marks.label: Proposed rate
marks.text: The new loan’s rate type, index and spread — see “The proposed rate and amount”.

marks.label: Proposed loan amount
marks.text: Type a smaller amount to test it. The line under it shows that loan’s coverage, LTV and debt yield.

marks.label: Can you? Yes
marks.text: The property supports at least what you owe.

marks.label: How “supports $X” is worked out
marks.text: The NOI, rate, payment and value behind the figure, and the lender’s four limits — see “How much the property supports”.

marks.label: Should you? Your decision
marks.text: The interest saved is less than the penalty, but the cash out is more than 20% of what you owe.

marks.label: Refinance now — with $X cash
marks.text: The cash left after paying off what you owe and the penalty. To take it, save the proposed loan (“Save as a loan — Refinance now” at the top).

marks.label: Wait until …
marks.text: Or keep today’s loan until it ends — nothing changes.

marks.label: Your decision.
marks.text: The choice is yours. Lowering the amount so far that the cash no longer covers the penalty is refused with “You can’t do that”.

steps.title: Don’t refinance
steps.text: The Mint: the property supports less than you owe, and its loan doesn’t end or reset within 12 months — so there is nothing to do yet.

marks.label: Don’t refinance
marks.text: The answer.

marks.label: You owe (payoff)
marks.text: What a new loan has to pay off.

marks.label: Property supports
marks.text: The biggest loan the property supports at the proposed rate and the lender’s limits.

marks.label: Today’s loan rate
marks.text: The rate today’s loan charges now.

marks.label: Proposed loan rate
marks.text: The new loan’s rate, from the rate boxes below.

marks.label: Proposed rate
marks.text: The new loan’s rate type, index and spread — see “The proposed rate and amount”.

marks.label: Proposed loan amount
marks.text: Type a smaller amount to test it. The line under it shows that loan’s coverage, LTV and debt yield.

marks.label: Can you? No
marks.text: What caps it, and what would change it: NOI rising, the rate falling, or a pay-down.

marks.label: How “supports $X” is worked out
marks.text: The NOI, rate, payment and value behind the figure, and the lender’s four limits — see “How much the property supports”.

marks.label: Bottom line
marks.text: Don’t refinance — the property can’t support a loan the size of the payoff yet.

steps.title: Can’t judge this yet
steps.text: A loan whose property has no NOI (no T12, nothing typed) can’t be sized. The box says so instead of guessing; the rate boxes are still there.

marks.label: Can’t judge this yet
marks.text: There is no NOI to size the refinance on.

marks.label: What to do
marks.text: Type the NOI with “Edit inputs” (Coverage & value, above), or upload the property’s T12 in Underwriting.

marks.label: Proposed rate
marks.text: The new loan’s rate type, index and spread — they still work without an NOI.

marks.label: Proposed loan amount
marks.text: Still there: type an amount and the rate boxes above it, and the proposed loan below still works out its payment.

topics.title: The proposed rate and amount
topics.intro: Inside the verdict box: the new loan’s rate type, its index and spread, and the amount.

steps.title: Hybrid — a fixed period, then adjustable
steps.text: The proposed loan starts from today’s loan’s type and a typical spread. Type your lender’s quote in the spread boxes; everything above and below updates at once.

marks.label: Fixed
marks.text: One rate for the whole term: a Treasury matched to the term + the lender’s spread.

marks.label: Floating
marks.text: An index (SOFR, Prime …) + a margin, changing as the index moves.

marks.label: Hybrid
marks.text: Fixed for the first years, then adjustable.

marks.label: Index (fixed period)
marks.text: The Treasury the fixed period is priced on. The list holds every rate the app has; “Fetch live rate” at the top refreshes them.

marks.label: Spread (bps)
marks.text: Type the lender’s quote in basis points (100 bps = 1%).

marks.label: Index (adjustable)
marks.text: What the rate follows after the fixed period.

marks.label: Margin (bps)
marks.text: The lender’s margin over that index.

marks.label: Proposed loan amount
marks.text: Up to what the property supports; lowering it shows the cash you’d pay in.

marks.label: Rate (fixed period)
marks.text: The rate worked out: the index today + the spread. “Built-in rate — fetch to update” means the index is the app’s own figure until you press “Fetch live rate”. The yellow “starting spread” tag says where the starting spread came from (your recent loans of this kind); it goes once you type the lender’s quote.

marks.label: Monthly payment (fixed period)
marks.text: The payment in the fixed years — the verdict and the limits use this rate.

marks.label: Monthly payment (after)
marks.text: The payment after the fixed period if the index stays where it is today — for information only.

marks.label: At this amount
marks.text: The proposed loan’s own coverage, interest-only coverage, LTV and debt yield at the amount typed.

steps.title: Floating
steps.text: Floating: pick the index and type the lender’s margin. The rate shown is today’s index + the margin.

marks.label: Floating
marks.text: Picked.

marks.label: Index
marks.text: SOFR (overnight or 30-day average), Prime, or a Treasury — every rate the app has.

marks.label: Spread (bps)
marks.text: The lender’s margin over the index, in basis points.

marks.label: Rate floor (%)
marks.text: The lowest the rate can go, whatever the index does. Empty = no floor.

marks.label: Rate cap (%)
marks.text: The highest the rate can go. Empty = no cap.

marks.label: Cap cost (bps/yr)
marks.text: The yearly cost of buying an interest-rate cap, which floating lenders often require. It starts at 0 — a cap costs nothing here until you buy one.

marks.label: Rate
marks.text: Today’s index (and the day it was set) + the spread.

marks.label: Proposed loan amount
marks.text: The amount of the new loan; switching the rate type works out what the property supports again.

steps.title: Fixed
steps.text: Fixed: the Treasury that matches the term, plus the lender’s spread.

marks.label: Fixed
marks.text: Picked.

marks.label: Index
marks.text: The Treasury matched to the loan’s term (change it if the lender prices on another).

marks.label: Spread (bps)
marks.text: The lender’s spread.

marks.label: Rate
marks.text: The Treasury today + the spread — one rate for the whole term.

marks.label: Proposed loan amount
marks.text: The amount of the new loan.

marks.label: At this amount
marks.text: That loan’s coverage, LTV and debt yield.

topics.title: How much the property supports
topics.intro: How “supports $X” is worked out: the NOI, the rate, the payment, the value — and the four limits a lender sizes a loan on.

steps.title: How “supports $X” is worked out
steps.text: Four limits each allow a loan; the smallest of the ones your lender uses is what the property supports. Type your lender’s own figures — they are kept with this refinance for the whole team.

marks.label: NOI
marks.text: The NOI used, and where it comes from.

marks.label: Rate
marks.text: The proposed loan’s rate (index + spread).

marks.label: Payment
marks.text: How the payment is figured (amortizing, interest-only months).

marks.label: Value
marks.text: NOI ÷ cap rate — or the appraisal, once you type one. The loan-to-value limit works on this.

marks.label: Appraised value
marks.text: Type an appraisal to use it instead of NOI ÷ cap rate.

marks.label: Dated
marks.text: The appraisal’s date (kept with it).

marks.label: Note
marks.text: Who appraised it, or any note.

marks.label: Lender preset
marks.text: Pick a lender’s saved limits (the topic “Lender presets”).

marks.label: Lender uses
marks.text: Tick the limits this lender actually uses; an unticked one is greyed and doesn’t count.

marks.label: Lender limit
marks.text: The limit’s name, how its loan is worked out, and (grey) that loan’s coverage, LTV and debt yield.

marks.label: Debt coverage, amortizing
marks.text: NOI ÷ (this × the loan constant). Lenders often ask 1.20–1.35×.

marks.label: Debt coverage, interest-only
marks.text: Leave blank (not used) unless the lender sizes on the interest-only payment.

marks.label: Loan-to-value
marks.text: The most it lends as a % of the value.

marks.label: Debt yield
marks.text: The least NOI ÷ loan it accepts.

marks.label: Loan it allows
marks.text: The biggest loan each limit allows on its own.

marks.label: Binds
marks.text: The limit that sets the amount — the smallest one used.

marks.label: The smallest
marks.text: The smallest loan of the limits used: what the property supports.

marks.label: Headroom
marks.text: How much room is left before the next limit would bind instead.

marks.label: Change history
marks.text: Every change to this refinance’s limits, appraisal and deal: when, who, old → new.

steps.title: An appraisal and the lender’s own limits
steps.text: Typed: an appraised value (a made-up $65,000,000), and Debt yield unticked because this lender doesn’t use it. The loan-to-value now works on the appraisal, and the unticked line is greyed.

marks.label: Value
marks.text: Now the appraisal, with its note.

marks.label: Use NOI ÷ cap rate instead
marks.text: Drops the appraisal and goes back to the value from NOI ÷ cap rate.

marks.label: Appraised value
marks.text: Clear the box to go back to NOI ÷ cap rate.

marks.label: Note
marks.text: Here “Example appraiser (made-up)”.

marks.label: Loan-to-value
marks.text: 75% of the appraisal.

marks.label: Not used by this lender
marks.text: Greyed; it no longer counts. Tick it to use it again. (At least one limit must stay ticked.)

marks.label: The smallest of the limits this lender uses
marks.text: Now only the ticked limits count.

marks.label: Back to the start
marks.text: Puts the limits back to 1.25× / 75% / 7%, all used. Shown once you have changed them.

marks.label: Change history
marks.text: The changes just made are listed here (next step).

steps.title: Change history
steps.text: Every change to this refinance — limits, appraisal, kind of deal, extension terms — with who made it and when.

marks.label: Refinance — change history
marks.text: This refinance’s own list.

marks.label: A change
marks.text: When, what (for example Refinance · appraised value), old → new, who, and where it came from.
Closes the list.

topics.title: Lender presets
topics.intro: A list of lenders’ limits kept for the whole group, so you pick a lender instead of typing its numbers. Only the group’s admin edits the list.

steps.title: Add a preset
steps.text: The list starts empty. Next to “Lender preset”, the admin sees “Add a preset” (later “Manage presets”).

marks.label: none yet
marks.text: No presets in the group’s list yet.

marks.label: Add a preset
marks.text: Opens the group’s list of lender presets. Only the group’s admin can change it — anyone else gets “Only the group’s admin changes the lender presets”.

marks.label: The limits
marks.text: Without a preset you type the lender’s limits here yourself.

steps.title: The presets window
steps.text: Each preset is one lender: its limits and which it uses, how it sizes an all-interest-only loan, the rate types it allows, its longest amortization, its usual penalty on an extension, notes and the source. Nothing is saved until “Save the list”.

marks.label: Name
marks.text: The lender, for example Fannie Mae. A preset without a name is dropped when you save.

marks.label: DSCR
marks.text: Its debt coverage on the amortizing payment.

marks.label: IO
marks.text: Its coverage on an interest-only payment (blank if it doesn’t use one).

marks.label: LTV
marks.text: Its most loan-to-value, in %.

marks.label: DY
marks.text: Its least debt yield, in %.

marks.label: Remove
marks.text: Takes this preset off the list.

marks.label: Uses
marks.text: Tick the limits this lender uses.

marks.label: Interest-only sizing
marks.text: Tick if it sizes a loan that is interest-only for its whole term on the interest-only payment.

marks.label: Rate types
marks.text: The rate types it lends at; an unticked one is greyed in the refinance.

marks.label: Longest amortization
marks.text: In years.

marks.label: Penalty on an extension
marks.text: What this lender usually asks when it extends a loan: the full penalty, on the pay-down only, a part (% or $), or none.

marks.label: Part (%)
marks.text: For “a part (%)”: the share of the full penalty (here 50%). “A part ($)” asks for a dollar amount instead.

marks.label: Notes
marks.text: Anything else worth remembering about this lender.

marks.label: Source
marks.text: Where the numbers came from, and when.

marks.label: Add a preset
marks.text: Adds another lender.

marks.label: Save the list
marks.text: Saves the list for the whole group and closes the window.

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Closes without saving — the changes are dropped.

steps.title: Picking a preset
steps.text: Saved, then picked for this refinance: the limits fill in from the preset, the table says which preset it is, and a rate type the lender doesn’t allow is greyed.

marks.label: Lender preset
marks.text: Pick a lender (or “None — type the limits”).

marks.label: Its name
marks.text: The preset in use — “(changed here)” once you change a limit by hand. Also the rate types it allows and its longest amortization.

marks.label: Manage presets
marks.text: Edit the group’s list (admin only).

marks.label: What it allows
marks.text: The rate types this lender lends at, and its longest amortization.

marks.label: The limits
marks.text: Filled from the preset (here 1.30× / 70% / 8%). Type over one and the chip says “changed here”.

marks.label: What the property supports
marks.text: Worked out again on the preset’s limits.

steps.title: A rate type the lender doesn’t allow
steps.text: The preset doesn’t allow floating, so “Floating” is greyed in the rate boxes; clicking it says why instead of switching.

marks.label: Floating (greyed)
marks.text: Not allowed by this lender’s preset. Clicking it shows “Example Agency (made-up): no floating” and nothing changes.

marks.label: Fixed
marks.text: Allowed.

marks.label: Hybrid
marks.text: Allowed.

topics.title: The proposed new loan
topics.intro: When the answer is Refinance (or your decision, or a pay-down), the proposed loan appears with its terms and its payment schedule.

steps.title: Proposed New Loan
steps.text: The proposed loan matches today’s term and interest-only period, priced at today’s rate. Every box is editable; the verdict above updates as you type.

marks.label: Loan amount
marks.text: Set in the verdict box above.

marks.label: Term (yrs)
marks.text: Years until the new loan is due.

marks.label: Amortization (yrs)
marks.text: Years the payment is figured over.

marks.label: Interest-only (mo)
marks.text: Months of interest-only payments first.

marks.label: Closing (% of loan)
marks.text: Closing costs, as a % of the loan.

marks.label: New monthly payment
marks.text: The first payment, and how it compares with today’s.

marks.label: vs your current
marks.text: Today’s monthly payment, and how much the new one saves (or costs) each month.

marks.label: Escrows & reserves
marks.text: Click to open: tax and insurance escrows, replacement and TI/LC reserves, ground lease, other escrows.

marks.label: Additional fees
marks.text: Click to open: servicing, trustee and other fees.

marks.label: Amortization schedule
marks.text: Every payment of the new loan, month by month: rate, interest, payment, principal and balance; interest-only months are marked IO. Scroll inside the box for the rest.

steps.title: Escrows, reserves and fees
steps.text: Opened: the monthly escrows and reserves, and the fees, that come with the new loan’s payment.

marks.label: Tax escrow
marks.text: Monthly real-estate-tax escrow, in dollars a month. Every box here is added to the new loan’s monthly payment.

marks.label: Insurance escrow
marks.text: Monthly insurance escrow.

marks.label: Replacement reserve
marks.text: Monthly replacement reserve.

marks.label: TI/LC reserve
marks.text: Tenant improvements and leasing commissions (commercial).

marks.label: Ground lease
marks.text: A ground-lease payment, if any.

marks.label: Servicing fee
marks.text: The servicer’s monthly fee.

marks.label: Other escrow 1
marks.text: Any other monthly escrow.

marks.label: Other escrow 2
marks.text: A second one.

marks.label: Trustee fee
marks.text: The trustee’s monthly fee.

marks.label: Other fee 1
marks.text: Any other monthly fee.

marks.label: Other fee 2
marks.text: A second one.

topics.title: Save as a loan
topics.intro: Saving the refinance makes the proposed loan a real loan and marks today’s loan paid off.

steps.title: It asks first
steps.text: “Save as a loan” shows what will happen before anything changes. Today’s loan becomes Paid off (refinanced) and leaves the totals; the new loan is added with today’s date. A pay-down is recorded on the new loan.

marks.label: Save the refinance?
marks.text: The question.

marks.label: What happens
marks.text: The new loan, the old loan(s) paid off, and any cash paid in.

marks.label: Save the refinance
marks.text: Does it. (Today’s loan can be restored from “Removed & paid-off loans” on the Portfolio tab.)

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Nothing changes.

topics.title: Extend with today’s lender
topics.intro: Instead of a new loan: today’s lender keeps the loan on new terms — usually after a pay-down so it fits the lender’s limits.

steps.title: Pick “Extend with today’s lender”
steps.text: Everything below now judges the extension: its own verdict, its rate, its limits and its terms. “Save the extension” appears at the top when the answer is Extend.

marks.label: Extend with today’s lender
marks.text: Picked.

marks.label: Save the extension
marks.text: Saves the extension on today’s loan (it asks first) — with the pay-down it needs.

steps.title: The extension’s verdict
steps.text: The same rule as a new loan, applied to the extension: the pay-down it needs to fit today’s lender’s limits, and whether it is worth doing.

marks.label: The answer
marks.text: Extend — pay down $X (or Not yet, or Don’t extend now).

marks.label: You’ll owe on …
marks.text: What you will owe on the day today’s terms end.

marks.label: Today’s lender allows
marks.text: The biggest loan today’s lender’s limits allow at the extension’s rate.

marks.label: Today’s loan rate
marks.text: With the reset ahead.

marks.label: Extension rate
marks.text: The index + today’s lender’s spread.

marks.label: Index
marks.text: What the extension’s rate floats on — every rate the app has.

marks.label: Spread (bps)
marks.text: Today’s lender’s quote over the index.

marks.label: Can you?
marks.text: Yes — with or without a pay-down.

marks.label: The pay-down
marks.text: What you will owe less what the lender’s limits allow, and which limit sets it.

marks.label: Today’s lender’s limits
marks.text: The limits table for the extension — kept apart from a new loan’s (next step).

marks.label: Should you?
marks.text: Yes when today’s loan ends or resets within 12 months; “Not yet” when nothing ends or resets within 12 months; otherwise yes only when the lower rate saves more than the penalty.

marks.label: Bottom line
marks.text: What to do, with the cash it takes: pay-down + penalty + fee.

steps.title: Today’s lender’s limits
steps.text: Type today’s lender’s own limits for the extension (here 1.11× amortizing and 1.35× interest-only, made-up). They are kept with the property, separately from a new loan’s.

marks.label: Amortizing coverage
marks.text: Today’s lender’s DSCR.

marks.label: Interest-only coverage
marks.text: Its coverage on the interest-only payment.

marks.label: Loan-to-value
marks.text: Today’s lender’s most loan-to-value — here on the appraisal typed above.

marks.label: Debt yield
marks.text: Its least debt yield.

marks.label: Lender uses
marks.text: Untick a limit today’s lender doesn’t use.

marks.label: Lender preset
marks.text: Pick today’s lender’s preset, if the group has one (“Manage presets” edits the list — admin only).

marks.label: Appraised value
marks.text: Shared with the new loan’s: one appraisal for the property (here a made-up $65,000,000).

marks.label: What today’s lender allows
marks.text: The smallest of the limits it uses; the binding one is marked BINDS.

marks.label: Interest-only hint
marks.text: The extension is interest-only for its whole term: untick the amortizing line if the lender sizes on the interest-only payment.

marks.label: Back to the new loan’s limits
marks.text: Drops today’s lender’s own limits and uses the new loan’s again.

marks.label: Change history
marks.text: Every change to the refinance, these limits included.

steps.title: The extension’s terms
steps.text: When today’s terms end, how long the new terms run, interest-only, the amortization after it, the lender’s penalty and the fee — and what it all adds up to.

marks.label: Today’s terms end on
marks.text: Starts at the payment before the rate resets (or the maturity).

marks.label: Months on the new terms
marks.text: How long the extension runs.

marks.label: Interest-only
marks.text: The whole term, the first N months, or none.

marks.label: Amortization
marks.text: Months the payment is figured over after interest-only.

marks.label: Early-payoff penalty
marks.text: What this lender asks: the full penalty, on the pay-down only, a part, or none. Until you pick, it assumes “on the pay-down”.

marks.label: Extension fee in
marks.text: % of the extended amount, or dollars.

marks.label: Extension fee
marks.text: The fee.

marks.label: Pay-down needed
marks.text: What you pay down so the loan fits the lender’s limits.

marks.label: Extended amount
marks.text: What you owe after the pay-down.

marks.label: At this amount
marks.text: The extended loan’s coverage, interest-only coverage, LTV and debt yield.

marks.label: Penalty
marks.text: In dollars, how it was worked out, and the full penalty today.

marks.label: Assumed
marks.text: Until you pick what this lender asks, the penalty is assumed to be on the pay-down only — confirm it with the lender.

marks.label: Extension fee
marks.text: The fee in dollars.

marks.label: Cash needed
marks.text: Pay-down + penalty + fee.

marks.label: First payment
marks.text: The date and amount of the first payment on the new terms.

marks.label: New maturity
marks.text: When the extended loan is due.

marks.label: Earlier than today’s
marks.text: A warning: these terms would end before today’s loan does. Type more months if that isn’t what you mean.

steps.title: Penalty: a part of it
steps.text: Picking “a part (%)” asks what share of the full penalty the lender wants; “a part ($)” asks for the dollar figure. “The first N months” of interest-only asks how many months.

marks.label: Part of the full penalty (%)
marks.text: Here 40% of today’s full penalty.

marks.label: Interest-only months
marks.text: How many months are interest-only (it appears when you pick “The first N months”).

marks.label: Penalty
marks.text: Now 40% of the full penalty — no longer “assumed”.

marks.label: Cash needed
marks.text: Follows at once.

steps.title: Penalty and fee in dollars
steps.text: “A part — a dollar amount” asks for the penalty the lender quotes, in dollars; the fee can be dollars too. Here a made-up $100,000 penalty and a $25,000 fee.

marks.label: A part — a dollar amount
marks.text: The other choices: the full penalty, on the pay-down only, a part (%), none.

marks.label: Penalty the lender asks ($)
marks.text: The lender’s figure.

marks.label: Extension fee in dollars
marks.text: Or % of the extended amount.

marks.label: Fee
marks.text: Counted in the cash needed.

steps.title: The payment schedule with the extension
steps.text: From today to the new maturity: the pay-down on the date today’s terms end, where the extension starts, and its months shaded.

marks.label: From today to …
marks.text: The whole schedule with the extension in place.

marks.label: Paid down
marks.text: The pay-down, as a principal payment.

marks.label: Extension starts
marks.text: The first payment on the new terms.

marks.label: Extension months
marks.text: Shaded: the new rate and terms.

steps.title: Save the extension
steps.text: It asks first. Today’s loan stays the same record: from the date its terms end, the new rate and term; the pay-down becomes a principal payment; the status becomes Extended. Every changed field goes into the loan’s history.

marks.label: Save the extension?
marks.text: The question.

marks.label: What happens
marks.text: The new terms, the pay-down, the penalty, the new maturity, the status and the cash needed.

marks.label: Save the extension
marks.text: Saves it.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Nothing changes.

steps.title: Saved — with Undo
steps.text: The refinance now shows the saved extension. “Undo the extension” puts today’s loan back exactly as it was (it asks first); “Change history” lists what changed.

marks.label: Extended with today’s lender
marks.text: The extension is saved on today’s loan.

marks.label: Saved
marks.text: When, and by whom. The loan’s schedule (on its own page too) now has the extension.

marks.label: What was saved
marks.text: The new terms, the pay-down, the new maturity and the cash it took.

marks.label: Undo the extension
marks.text: Restores today’s loan exactly as before the extension (it asks first).

marks.label: Change history
marks.text: The refinance’s history — the extension and every change before it.

steps.title: Undo
steps.text: Undo asks first, then puts back the rate, the maturity, the status and the schedule. The undo is in the history too.

marks.label: Undo the extension?
marks.text: The question.

marks.label: What happens
marks.text: The loan goes back to its terms before the extension; the pay-down comes off the schedule; the history keeps both.

marks.label: Undo
marks.text: Does it.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Keeps the extension.

steps.title: Not yet
steps.text: The Mews at Princeton: today’s lender’s limits cover what you’ll owe, but nothing ends or resets within 12 months — so “Not yet”, and there is no “Save the extension” button. (When a lower rate doesn’t pay for the penalty, the answer is “Don’t extend now”.)

marks.label: Not yet
marks.text: Today’s terms end more than 12 months from now.

marks.label: Can you? Yes
marks.text: Today’s lender’s limits allow more than you’ll owe — no pay-down needed.

marks.label: Should you? Not yet
marks.text: When today’s terms end, and that nothing ends or resets within 12 months.

marks.label: Bottom line
marks.text: Not yet — decide closer to the date.

topics.title: Several loans or properties together
topics.intro: A property with a senior and a mezzanine loan refinances as one package; “Create a portfolio…” puts several properties under one new loan.

steps.title: Senior + mezz — the whole property
steps.text: Pick the property’s combined entry (“2 loans”) under Specific Property, then Refi Calculator: both loans are paid off by one new loan. Here Avalon White Plains, with a made-up NOI typed for the example.

marks.label: The loans
marks.text: Every loan on the property, refinanced together (they depend on one another).

marks.label: Payoff balance
marks.text: Each loan at its own balance, added up.

marks.label: Monthly payments
marks.text: Today’s payments on all of them.

marks.label: Current rate
marks.text: The loans’ rate together, weighted by what is owed on each.

marks.label: Remaining
marks.text: Months until the first of them ends.

marks.label: Matures
marks.text: When the first of them is due.

steps.title: Create a portfolio…
steps.text: On the Portfolio tab, above the Coverage table: “Create a portfolio…”. Tick every property the one new loan will secure; the line under the list says how many loans it pays off and the NOI. Nothing changes until you save the new loan on the next screen.

marks.label: Find a property
marks.text: Type to narrow the list.

marks.label: Tick a property
marks.text: Tick each property the new loan will secure.

marks.label: Owes · NOI
marks.text: What is owed on the property, and its NOI with where it comes from.

marks.label: No NOI
marks.text: A property without a T12 or a typed NOI. You can still tick it, but the package can’t be sized until it has one.

marks.label: The package
marks.text: How many are ticked, the loans to pay off and what is owed, and the NOI together.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Closes the list.

marks.label: Create the portfolio
marks.text: Opens the refinance of the ticked properties together. It needs at least two, and at least one loan to pay off.

steps.title: The portfolio’s refinance
steps.text: The same refinance screen, for the whole package: NOI by property, with each one’s NOI and where it comes from. A property with no NOI can be typed in the table.

marks.label: A property
marks.text: One row per property in the package.

marks.label: NOI
marks.text: Its NOI.

marks.label: From
marks.text: Where the NOI comes from: a T12, your override, or typed on its loan.

marks.label: Together
marks.text: The NOI the package is sized on.

steps.title: The portfolio’s verdict
steps.text: “These 3 properties support …” — the verdict and everything after it work exactly as for one loan; “Save as a loan” puts one new loan on all of them and pays off every loan on them.

marks.label: The answer
marks.text: For the whole package — here a pay-down before Queens Gate’s rate resets.

marks.label: Which properties
marks.text: The properties and the number of loans paid off.

marks.label: You owe (payoff)
marks.text: Every loan on them, added up.

marks.label: Properties support
marks.text: The biggest single loan the properties support together.

marks.label: Today’s loan rate
marks.text: The loans’ rate together, weighted by what is owed (with the first reset ahead).

marks.label: Proposed loan rate
marks.text: The one new loan’s rate.

marks.label: When, and the pay-down
marks.text: What ends first, and the pay-down a new loan needs. (An extension isn’t offered for a package — it is a single loan’s choice.)

marks.label: Proposed rate
marks.text: The one new loan’s rate type, index and spread.

marks.label: Proposed loan amount
marks.text: The one new loan.

marks.label: Can you?
marks.text: For all of them together.

marks.label: How “supports $X” is worked out
marks.text: The package’s NOI (all of them together), the rate, the payment, the value and the limits.

marks.label: Bottom line
marks.text: What to do for the package.

steps.title: A property with no NOI
steps.text: Here Queens Gate Apartments and Avalon Norwalk, which has no T12 and no NOI typed. Counting it as $0 would understate what the package supports, so nothing is sized yet — type its NOI right in the table.

marks.label: With an NOI
marks.text: Queens Gate: its NOI and where it comes from.

marks.label: Type its NOI
marks.text: Avalon Norwalk has no T12 and nothing typed. Type its yearly NOI here — it is saved on the property, as if typed on its page — and the package is sized at once.

marks.label: Total
marks.text: Blank until every property has an NOI.

marks.label: What is missing
marks.text: Which properties have no NOI. Type 0 only if the property truly earns nothing.

steps.title: Can’t judge this yet — the package
steps.text: The verdict box names the property that has no NOI instead of guessing.

marks.label: Can’t judge this yet
marks.text: The package can’t be sized yet.

marks.label: No NOI for …
marks.text: Which property is missing its NOI, and what to do: upload its T12 or type its NOI in “NOI by property” above.

marks.label: Proposed rate
marks.text: Still there.

marks.label: Proposed loan amount
marks.text: Still there.
